_comment: Editorial copy for the interest pages, keyed by slug. Everything else on an
interest page is derived: the majors grid comes from briefs/programs-data.json
(filtered on the `interest` title below) and the college cards come from
briefs/colleges-schools-data.json (looked up by the `colleges` slugs below).
`interest` MUST match a title in programs-data.json's `interests` facet exactly.
Art & Performance, Business & Entrepreneurship, Communication & Literature,
Cultures & Languages, Data & Analysis, Design & Planning,
Human Behavior & Social Thought, Natural & Physical Sciences,
`careers` and `colleges` are hand-curated per interest -- neither is derivable
from the program data. `colleges` mirrors the live page's curated three.

engineering-technology.title: Engineering & Technology

hero.headline: Engineering & Technology
hero.text: Turn your passion for creating systems and structures through science and technology into a career.
hero.alt: The entrance to the Jeong H. Kim Engineering Building

intro.text: Students interested in Engineering and Technology programs will learn how to innovate the digital and physical world through science and technology.

majors.headline: Related Majors
majors.text: Students will learn how to make innovative scientific and technological contributions to an evolving world through research and experimentation to design, build and use an array of different systems, machines and structures.
majors.alt: Students working in the Glenn L. Martin wind tunnel

careers.headline: Careers in Engineering & Technology
careers.alt: A diver in the Neutral Buoyancy Research Facility tank

_alumni_comment: Optional. Omit the block and the page simply has no alumni carousel --
build-interest.py renders section 8 only when `alumni` is present.
Renders as umd-element-carousel-thumbnail, the same bordered 3-up person
strip as the sitewide Notable Alumni block on pages/academics/index.html.
The portrait is the card's own slot="image"; `thumbnail` mirrors it onto
the host for parity with that page (the v2 composite ignores the
attribute, but RULES §27 documents it and academics/index.html sets it).
`image` / `thumbnail` are optional per person: without them the card is
text-only in its bordered cell. Adding a portrait later is a data edit.
